subject: BrightLayer: streaming/chat timeouts causing 5xx/429 spike — exec escalation
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@brightlayer.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Cc: Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@brightlayer.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: spike in 5xx/429s and streaming timeouts — impacting chat UX

Hi Stephanie / Redwood team,

We started seeing a large uptick in 5xx and 429 responses starting around 07:45 PT this morning. The symptoms are: streaming/chat completions timing out mid-stream (client gets idle stream disconnect), clients retry aggressively which then drives additional 429s. Our CS dashboard shows a 15% drop in successful streams over the past 90 minutes and several of our customer-facing chat sessions were effectively disconnected.

I've attached a p99_latency_graph.png and a short trace dump (streaming-trace-20260321.log). We need immediate help — this is already an exec-level issue for us (Brian is cc'd). Can someone confirm whether this is a Redwood runtime issue or if our SDK is misbehaving? We didn't deploy anything new on our side.

Requested next steps from our side: short call + timeline for mitigation, and visibility into whether this will trigger any SLA credits.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Customer Success Manager, BrightLayer

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-21T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: BrightLayer streaming timeouts — needs exec attention

Team — BrightLayer (large PLG customer, renewal Q4) is experiencing streaming/chat timeouts that are leading to a retry storm and elevated 5xx/429 rates. Customer execs are involved. Quick summary:
- Customer reported spike started ~07:45 PT (attached p99 graph).
- Symptoms: idle stream disconnects on client -> client retries -> spikes in concurrent open connections -> 429s and 5xx from backend.
- Business impact: customer-facing chat UX failing; they flagged potential renewal impact.

Preliminary technical hypotheses:
1) Client-side timeouts + aggressive retry behavior causing a retry storm localized to their API key.
2) Runtime idle-stream handling bug: our server sometimes leaves stale KV cache / connection state and doesn't free socket slots quickly, preventing autoscaler from recovering fast enough.
3) Batching/quota throttles misapplied under sudden concurrent streaming load (config + circuit breaker interplay).

Short-term mitigations I propose we implement immediately:
- Enable per-key circuit breaker (limit concurrent streams) for BrightLayer while we troubleshoot
- Reduce server idle-stream timeout from 60s -> 20s for affected endpoint to free resources faster
- Temporarily increase autoscale headroom on the dedicated pool (if applicable)

Can Rishi confirm which of these we can flip in the next 15 minutes? Also, Marissa — we need an exec-facing note and a proposed customer credit amount to offer immediately if we can't contain impact within 1 hour.

Thanks,
Stephanie

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: BrightLayer streaming timeouts — needs exec attention

Investigating now. Quick findings from Prometheus/tracing and the attached stream traces:
- Correlation: 429 rate correlates strongly with a surge in concurrent open streaming connections from BrightLayer's API key between 07:40-08:55 PT.
- Runtime telemetry: some backend workers show long-lived connections that are not releasing KV cache references after EOF (we see EOF but process doesn't call free path due to edge case where client-side FIN isn't being handled for idle streams).
- SDK behavior: customer-side SDK versions earlier than 1.4.2 have aggressive retry short-circuiting; their fleet shows many clients retrying with minimal backoff.

Immediate actions I can perform (now):
1) Flip per-key circuit breaker to cap concurrent streams at 200 for BrightLayer (can be backfilled to 400 once stable) — ETA 5 min to apply.
2) Reduce streaming idle timeout from 60s -> 20s at the load-balancer/runtime for affected cluster — ETA 10 min.
3) Deploy temporary ingress rule to favor their traffic to new autoscale group (needs ops signoff) — ETA 20 min.

Longer term: patch runtime to correctly release KV cache on abrupt client disconnects (INF-9042). I will open a hotfix branch; ETA for PR: 24-48 hours.

I'll join the bridge in 5.

Rishi Malhotra
Lead Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Good triage — thanks. For exec comms to BrightLayer, suggested concise wording:

"Brian / Sarah — we apologize for the disruption. Our SRE team has identified a coupling between an increase in concurrent streaming sessions and an idle-stream handling bug in our runtime that can, in edge cases, delay resource reclamation. We have enacted immediate mitigations (per-key circuit breaker, reduced idle timeout, increased headroom). Our SREs are executing a hotfix and will provide an ETA for full resolution. We will follow up with a formal incident summary and a proposed credit."

Proposed short-term credit: offer 10% service credit for the affected week and a technical post-mortem within 72 hours. If they request more we can escalate to executive approval.

I'll prepare the exec note and standby for the bridge.

Marissa Cole
VP Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
